niche.habitat: Planetary surfaces under 1G loading, spanning diverse biomes from tropical jungles to arid deserts and shallow seas.
niche.diet: Omnivorous, optimized for high-gravity digestion and nutrient density, supplemented by cultivated crops.
niche.active: Diurnal, aligned with host star cycles and agricultural/territorial maintenance schedules.

body: Robust, weight-bearing frames with dense, reinforced skeletal structures counteract compressive loading, while compact cranial volumes reduce metabolic overhead in high-gravity environments. Their divergent anatomy often features elaborate veils and headgear, serving as both status markers and thermal regulators.

skill.effect: Uses planetary mass to ground attacks and stabilize allies in combat, granting +2 to balance checks and reducing knockback distance by 4 meters for 3 turns.

chains.weakness: Immune to microgravity; become sluggish and disoriented in void environments, suffering disadvantage on agility checks until they find mass to brace against.

relations.note: Zero-g lets Asteromorph brains bloom into sails; 1G forces Terrestrial skulls to stay compact and reinforced. Same root, opposite architecture. -> Skill: 'Cranial load tolerance' (Defence)

Subjects pump closed-loop gas-exchange cultures and modular biomass; Terrestrials provide 1G structural management and regulatory oversight. A mutualistic loop of flesh and gravity. -> Skill: 'Bio-infrastructure sync' (Social)

Terrestrials enforce 1G regulatory zones on planetary surfaces. New Machines use remodelable chassis to temporarily shed gravity-dependence, bypassing Terrestrial jurisdiction and operating in void niches. -> Skill: 'Gravity bypass' (Control)

temperament: Authoritative and pragmatic, they view themselves as stewards of planetary ecosystems and enforce stability through strict hierarchical control.
secrets: Can temporarily lower their bone density by secreting specialized enzymes, allowing brief periods of enhanced agility at the cost of structural vulnerability.
moments: Standing on a sun-drenched savanna, they adjust their dense skeletal alignment to absorb impact from leaping prey, their veiled forms casting long shadows that signal territorial dominance to subordinate species.
